subject: Stream quality & throughput spec + harness agreement
messages:
From: Priya Shah <priya.shah@acmeretail.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Subject: Post-demo: clarifying streaming targets & next steps

Thanks again for the demo today — the team found the streaming behavior promising. A few follow-ups from our side so we can scope the test window and internal sign-offs:

- Can you confirm latency targets for short-turn vs long-turn streaming? We need p95 and p99 for both.
- What concurrency/throughput should we aim for in the initial qualification run (baseline + burst)?
- We assume the harness will accept a canonical prompt set and a deterministic flag for model runs — can you share the exact artifacts?
- We will need a short measurement definition doc we can give to our infra and procurement.

Attaching our initial requirements spreadsheet (redacted). If you can reply with a recommended test plan and list of artifacts, we can lock a 48–72 hour window next week.

Attachments: acme_streaming_requirements.xlsx

Thanks,
Priya
Senior Engineering Manager, Acme Retail
perf@acmeretail.com

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: Priya Shah <priya.shah@acmeretail.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 4 Jul 2027 09:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: clarifying streaming targets & next steps

Hi Priya — great to sync. Below is a concise proposal to align the qualification run and the artifacts we'll hand off. I kept the definitions operational so your infra/procurement can use them directly.

1) Latency targets (streaming, token-level)
- Short-turn (<=64 tokens per request): p95 < 200 ms, p99 < 400 ms (end-to-end server-to-client token emission)
- Mid-turn (65–512 tokens): p95 < 350 ms, p99 < 700 ms
- Long-turn (>512 tokens): best-effort; report percentiles and tail behavior — we recommend measuring p50/p95/p99 per 100-token window.

2) Throughput & concurrency
- Baseline: 250 concurrent streams (typical shopping flow profile).
- Burst: 500 concurrent streams for up to 10 minutes to exercise autoscale/fallback paths.
- Sustained tokens/sec: target 1.2M tokens/sec cluster-wide for the qualification harness (we'll scale the pool to achieve this).

3) Streaming semantics & reproducibility
- Harness will play a canonicalized prompt set (attached: prompt_set_v2.csv). Prompts are deterministic; harness will set a fixed random seed and disable non-deterministic kernels where possible.
- KV-cache warm vs cold runs: we'll run both. Cold-run = empty cache; Warm-run = run warmup prefix per prompt.

4) Measurement definitions (attached short doc)
- "Token emission latency": measured from model ready-to-send to first client-visible token (includes network and server emission delay). We provide both server-side internal timestamps and client-side observed latencies.
- "Stream completeness": percent of streams delivering all expected tokens within the SLA window.
- Resource accounting: per-request GPU utilization, per-model QPS, memory-alloc peaks.

5) Artifacts we will deliver before the test
- harness_config.yaml (harness configuration + load profile)
- prompt_set_v2.csv (canonicalized prompts, with tags for short/mid/long)
- measurement_definitions_v1.pdf (definition table + collection points)
- repro_check.sh (simple script to validate deterministic run in your environment)

Next steps
- If this looks right, can Acme: (a) confirm the 48–72h window availability, (b) upload a redacted sample of production request traces (for shaping the prompt distribution), and (c) confirm whether we should instrument client-side timestamps?

--
Soojin Lee
Principal Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwood.com

- Ensure the harness runs with KV-cache behavior flagged; cold/warm runs are essential to reproduce tail latency.
- We'll include a short reproducibility checklist in repro_check.sh; it will validate deterministic kernels, fixed seeds, and GPU affinity.

Soojin
